project.title: Nudibranch
project.content:
A sea slug in bold black linework that comes alive: it floats, its limbs ripple like seaweed, and when you stir too fast it pulls them in and flares into warning colours, then slowly calms down again.

Real nudibranchs warn with colour – often of the poison they take from their food. This field guide follows six species of the invented genus Mikatoa, from the mint drifter to the ink ghost; each is coloured by what it eats, a pastel from this site at rest and a strong warning colour when alarmed. The motion is made in p5.js from the one drawing: every point turns around the body's spine as a wave travels along it, and the limb tips curl. A first version had a small neural network (Python, PyTorch) learn the frames between two hand-drawn poses – it's in the process below.

caseStudy.role: Solo project – drawing, motion design, code
caseStudy.challenge: Nudibranchs have been among my favourite sea animals since I started diving. I wanted my drawing of one to move the way they do – alive in the browser, without redrawing it frame by frame and without losing the bold linework.

decisions.title: Learned in-betweens first
decisions.text: I drew two poses of the limbs and trained a small PyTorch network to learn how each point of the outline moves from one to the other. It worked – but the result was a fixed loop, not a creature.

decisions.title: Motion from rules, not frames
decisions.text: The live version turns every point around the body's spine as a wave travels along it. The drawing stays one drawing, and the motion can react: stir too fast and it pulls its limbs in and flares into warning colours.

decisions.title: One system, six species
decisions.text: Colours and behaviour are parameters, so the same code makes six specimens – and renders the field-guide posters straight from the live sketch.

caseStudy.result: A live piece on this page that runs on phones and desktops, six A5 field-guide posters, and the source on GitHub.
